tagline: East from prairie into pine, lake country all the way.
intro: Highway 34 leaves Detroit Lakes heading east, and the country changes under it as it goes, prairie grassland in the west giving way to hardwoods and then conifer forest toward Park Rapids and Walker. From Park Rapids a spur runs north on Highway 71 to Itasca State Park and the source of the Mississippi, 88 miles of road in all.

People have been coming to these lakes on vacation for generations, and there are hundreds of lakeside resorts along the way. In June, showy lady's slippers bloom along the south side of 34 from around Height of Land Lake to east of Snellman.

moments.title: Itasca State Park
moments.text: The Mississippi leaves Lake Itasca over an outlet dam 44 feet long, in water shallow enough to wade, in a park the legislature created in 1891 by a single vote.

moments.title: Akeley
moments.text: T. B. Walker built his big sawmill here in 1902 and the town boomed, and a 25-foot Paul Bunyan now kneels beside a giant cradle.

moments.title: Walker
moments.text: Founded in 1896 and named for T. B. Walker in hopes of luring that sawmill, the town lost it to Akeley because his wife disapproved of its bars and brothels.
